title: Homestyle Aloo Tamatar Curry (Potato & Tomato Stew)
description: A fragrant, comforting North Indian curry made with tender potatoes, ripe juicy tomatoes, ginger, cumin, and mild spices. Perfect with warm rotis or steamed basmati rice.
ingredients: 2 medium ripe red tomatoes (pureed or finely chopped)
1 tsp grated ginger and minced garlic
1/2 tsp red chili powder or paprika
1 tbsp cold-pressed mustard oil or olive oil
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and allow them to crackle for 30 seconds.
Add minced onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden (about 4 minutes).
Stir in grated ginger, garlic, turmeric, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Sauté for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook down until tomatoes soften and oil gently separates from the gravy (about 5-6 minutes).
Add cubed potatoes and gently coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in water, cover with lid, and simmer on medium-low flame for 10 minutes until potatoes absorb flavors.
Lightly mash 2-3 potato chunks with the back of your spoon to naturally thicken the curry.
Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve piping hot.
substitutions: Potatoes: Can be substituted with sweet potatoes, cauliflower florets, or chickpeas.
Tomatoes: 1/2 cup canned crushed tomatoes or 2 tbsp tomato paste diluted in water.
Mustard oil: Can use ghee (if not vegan) or neutral avocado oil.
allergen_notes: Naturally gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, and soy-free.
storage_and_handling: Cool completely before transferring to an airtight glass container. Keeps refrigerated for up to 4 days. Reheat with 2 tbsp warm water as the potatoes will thicken the gravy over time.

title: Protein-Packed Palak Paneer (Spinach Cottage Cheese)
description: Silky spiced spinach puree tossed with lightly pan-seared paneer cubes, infused with garlic, cumin, and garam masala.
ingredients: 250g fresh baby spinach leaves (blanched in boiling water for 2 mins, then ice bath)
200g paneer cubes (or firm tofu for vegan option)
1 tbsp fresh cream or cashew cream (optional)
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, shock immediately in ice water to lock in vibrant green chlorophyll, then blend to a smooth puree.
In a skillet, lightly sear paneer cubes in 1 tsp oil until golden on edges (optional), then set aside.
In the same pan, heat remaining oil, add cumin seeds, and sauté minced garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add onions and cook until soft and golden brown. Add pureed tomato, turmeric, and salt. Cook until paste thickens.
Pour in the spinach puree, simmer on low heat for 3-4 minutes.
Gently fold in paneer cubes and garam masala. Simmer 2 more minutes.
Swirl in cream if desired. Serve with roti, naan, or jeera rice.
substitutions: Paneer: Firm pressed tofu (for a 100% vegan dairy-free alternative).
Cream: Unsweetened coconut cream or soaked cashew paste.
allergen_notes: Contains dairy (paneer, ghee, cream). Use tofu and coconut oil for dairy-free.
storage_and_handling: Store refrigerated in airtight container for up to 3 days. Do not over-boil when reheating to preserve color.

title: Mediterranean Quinoa Rainbow Power Bowl
description: Nutrient-loaded vegetarian power bowl featuring fluffy cooked quinoa, roasted chickpeas, diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, kalamata olives, and a zesty lemon-tahini vinaigrette.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked white or tricolor quinoa
1 cup canned chickpeas (rinsed, drained, and tossed with cumin and paprika)
2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley or mint
2 tbsp tahini or extra virgin olive oil
Salt and cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Roast seasoned chickpeas in an oven at 200°C (400°F) or pan-fry in a skillet for 8 minutes until crispy.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic, 2 tbsp warm water, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until a silky dressing forms.
Divide cooked quinoa between two wide serving bowls as the nutritious base.
Arrange crispy chickpeas, diced cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, and kalamata olives neatly over the quinoa.
Drizzle liberally with lemon-tahini dressing and garnish with chopped fresh herbs.
substitutions: Quinoa: Brown rice, farro, couscous, or riced cauliflower.
Tahini: Greek yogurt dill dressing or balsamic vinaigrette.
storage_and_handling: Components can be prepped up to 4 days ahead and stored separately in the fridge. Assemble and dress right before serving.

title: Herb Lemon Grilled Chicken & Steamed Broccoli
description: Tender grilled chicken breast marinated with oregano, rosemary, garlic, and fresh lemon juice, served alongside crisp-tender garlic steamed broccoli.
ingredients: 2 chicken breast fillets (approx. 180g each, lightly pounded to even thickness)
1/2 tsp sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: In a bowl, combine 1.5 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, minced garlic, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Coat chicken breasts evenly with marinade. Let sit at room temperature for 10-15 minutes.
Heat a grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts and sear without moving for 5-6 minutes.
Flip and cook for another 5-6 minutes until internal temperature registers 74°C (165°F). Transfer to a plate to rest for 5 minutes.
In a small covered pan, steam broccoli florets with 3 tbsp water and a pinch of salt for 4 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp.
Toss steamed broccoli with remaining olive oil and lemon squeeze. Slice chicken and serve together.
substitutions: Chicken: Turkey breast, salmon fillet, or thick-sliced portobello mushroom caps.
Broccoli: Asparagus spears, green beans, or zucchini coins.
storage_and_handling: Raw chicken handling: wash hands, sanitize surfaces, never wash raw poultry under faucet to avoid pathogen aerosolization. Cooked chicken lasts 4 days in refrigerator.

title: Hearty Golden Moong Dal & Spinach Khichdi
description: An ancient ayurvedic one-pot comfort dish combining yellow moong lentils, whole rice, baby spinach, cumin, and ginger tadka.
ingredients: 1/2 cup short-grain white or brown rice (rinsed)
instructions: Rinse dal and rice together under cold water until water runs clear.
In a pressure cooker or deep pot, heat ghee or oil. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add grated ginger, asafetida, and turmeric. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Add drained rice, dal, and 4 cups of water with salt.
If using pressure cooker, cook for 3 whistles. If using pot, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until porridge-like.
Stir in shredded fresh spinach during the final 3 minutes of cooking until wilted.
Serve warm with a spoon of fresh yogurt or pickle.
substitutions: Rice: Rolled oats, broken wheat (dalia), or quinoa.
Moong dal: Red masoor dal or split yellow peas.
allergen_notes: Gluten-free (ensure asafetida is compounded without wheat flour).
storage_and_handling: Refrigerates well for 3 days. Add hot water when reheating as lentils continue absorbing water.
